sections.title: Abstract

summary.text: Summarizes a pipeline for digitizing and segmenting ~831,000 scanned mathematical documents in zbMATH Open using Mathpix for LaTeX OCR and fine-tuned generative LLMs in a Majority Voting framework for document separation, achieving 97.5% text extraction accuracy (89.1% boundary index accuracy overall) and processing 810,977 documents into machine-readable text (721,288 with LaTeX boundary indexes).

sections.extract: This paper presents a specialized methodology for digitizing and segmenting mathematical documents from zbMATH Open, a com- prehensive database of mathematical literature, to enhance ma- chine processing capabilities. Currently, approximately 831,000 documents exist only in scanned volumes, which makes them not machine-processable. Furthermore, these scans often span multi- ple pages or share pages with other

sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the problem of converting ~831,000 historical scanned review entries in zbMATH Open (out of over 4.8 million total entries) into machine-readable LaTeX for mathematical information retrieval, noting the challenges of varying historical typesetting and multi-document or multi-page scan layouts illustrated in Figure 1.

sections.extract: Introduction Printed mathematical literature has a long history, with records dating back several centuries. Among the most comprehensive re- sources in the field, zbMATH Open (1868 – present) serves as a critical abstracting and reviewing service in pure and applied math- ematics [21]. summary.text: Reviews prior work on post-OCR document extraction and layout segmentation using regular expressions (Pitou et al., Pandey et al.), computer vision models including Faster-RCNN, U-Net, Segmentation Transformer, and Document Image Transformer (DiT), and NLP/LLM approaches using LSTM, BERT, and GPT-3.5.

The size of the context window was also critical. summary.text: Describes fine-tuning the three pre-trained LLMs using LoRA in LLaMA-Factory, selecting a learning rate of 0.0005 and 5 epochs via an 80/20 train/validation split of the 1,000-sample training dataset (with CalmExperiment-7B-slerp achieving the lowest validation loss), and then fine-tuning on all 1,000 training samples.

sections.title: Errors analysis

summary.text: Categorizes the 12 test-set errors made by the Majority Voting method into four causes: OCR formatting errors (2 cases), ambiguity between nearly identical neighboring titles (2 cases), LLM hallucinations on longer documents (4 cases), and metadata inclusion/omission errors (4 cases).

sections.extract: Errors analysis This section reviews the main sources of errors that occur when using the Majority Voting method and analyzes each type. By do- ing this, we can better understand the limitations of the current approach and guide further optimization efforts to improve the accuracy and reliability of document-splitting methods. • OCR formatting errors: an OCR error may cause the document to be processed incorrectly

sections.title: Error detection hypotheses

summary.text: Tests and refutes two standalone error-detection hypotheses on the 18 test errors of fine-tuned CalmExperiment-7B-slerp—showing neither Mathpix page confidence scores (Hypothesis 1) nor output token probabilities from LLaMA-Factory (Hypothesis 2) reliably predict segmentation errors—and describes Subsection 8.5's whitespace-normalized exact-matching method for recovering start and end character indexes in the raw LaTeX OCR output (succeeding on 90.6% of the test set with 98.4% accuracy, or 89.1% overall while filtering out hallucinations).

sections.extract: Error detection hypotheses In addition to analyzing specific types of errors, we tested two hypotheses to identify potential indicators of errors in the document splitting process. These hypotheses focus on aspects of OCR quality and the probabilistic nature of Transformers-based Large Language Models, aiming to establish methods for error detection. sections.title: All data processing

summary.text: Reports applying the Majority Voting pipeline to all 810,977 eligible zbMATH Open documents (differing from CalmExperiment-7B-slerp alone in 3.4% of cases) and recovering exact start and end character indexes in the LaTeX scans for 721,288 documents (88.9%).

sections.extract: All data processing After achieving a high accuracy score on the test dataset, the next step was to use the best approach we had created on the entire dataset. Thus, we applied the Majority Voting approach to 810,977 elements in the zbMATH Open table, finishing the transformation of these mathematical documents into machine-readable and search- able formats as a practical outcome of this research. sections.title: Conclusion

summary.text: Concludes by summarizing the Mathpix LaTeX OCR conversion of 252,624 zbMATH Open pages, the 97.5% test accuracy of the three-LLM Majority Voting splitter (and 89.1% overall index accuracy), the public release of code, models, and datasets on GitHub, Zenodo, and Hugging Face, and DFG funding acknowledgments.

sections.extract: Conclusion This project successfully identified the optimal OCR tool, Mathpix, for converting scanned pages to LaTeX format, using the BLEU Score and Edit Distance metrics. As the next step, 252,624 scanned pages from zbMATH Open were converted into LaTeX. narratives.en: Figure 5, 'Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time': training loss (log scale, ~5e-4 to 0.2) against epoch (0-5) for CalmExperiment-7B-slerp (red), Maxine-7B-0401-stock (blue), Mistral-Passthrough-8L-10B (green). All three are noisy and trend downward from about 0.17 (green near 0.04) to about 10^-3.
narratives.fr: Figure 5, « Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time » : perte d'entraînement (échelle logarithmique, ~5e-4 à 0,2) en fonction de l'époque (0–5) pour CalmExperiment-7B-slerp (rouge), Maxine-7B-0401-stock (bleu) et Mistral-Passthrough-8L-10B (vert). Les trois courbes sont bruitées et suivent une tendance baissière d'environ 0,17 (vert près de 0,04) jusqu'à environ 10^-3.
narratives.es: Figura 5, «Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time»: pérdida de entrenamiento (escala logarítmica, ~5e-4 a 0.2) frente a la época (0–5) para CalmExperiment-7B-slerp (rojo), Maxine-7B-0401-stock (azul) y Mistral-Passthrough-8L-10B (verde). Las tres curvas presentan ruido y muestran una tendencia descendente desde aproximadamente 0.17 (la verde cerca de 0.04) hasta aproximadamente 10^-3.
narratives.ar: الشكل 5، 'Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time': خسارة التدريب (بمقياس لوغاريتمي، من نحو 5e-4 إلى 0.2) مقابل الحقب التدريبية (0–5) لنماذج CalmExperiment-7B-slerp (أحمر) وMaxine-7B-0401-stock (أزرق) وMistral-Passthrough-8L-10B (أخضر). تتسم المنحنيات الثلاثة بالتذبذب وتتجه هبوطاً من نحو 0.17 (والأخضر قرب 0.04) إلى نحو 10^-3.
narratives.ru: Рисунок 5, «Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time»: потери при обучении (логарифмическая шкала, от ~5e-4 до 0,2) в зависимости от эпохи (0–5) для моделей CalmExperiment-7B-slerp (красный), Maxine-7B-0401-stock (синий) и Mistral-Passthrough-8L-10B (зелёный). Все три кривые зашумлены и демонстрируют нисходящий тренд примерно от 0,17 (зелёная — около 0,04) до ~10^-3.
narratives.zh: 图 5“Logarithmic Plot of Training Losses over Time”：CalmExperiment-7B-slerp（红）、Maxine-7B-0401-stock（蓝）与 Mistral-Passthrough-8L-10B（绿）的训练损失（对数刻度，约 5e-4 至 0.2）随训练轮次（0–5）的变化。三条曲线均存在波动，整体从约 0.17（绿线约为 0.04）呈下降趋势至约 10^-3。

narratives.en: Figure 6: scan of review page 35 where the computer-vision model has drawn one red box (labelled 'title') around the Fröhlich and Shepherdson title line; the other two titles on the page (Yoshida, Auslander and Buchsbaum) are not boxed.
narratives.fr: Figure 6 : numérisation de la page 35 de recensions où le modèle de vision par ordinateur a tracé un seul cadre rouge (étiqueté « title ») autour de la ligne de titre de Fröhlich et Shepherdson ; les deux autres titres de la page (Yoshida, Auslander et Buchsbaum) ne sont pas encadrés.
narratives.es: Figura 6: escaneo de la página 35 de reseñas donde el modelo de visión por computador ha trazado un único recuadro rojo (etiquetado como «title») alrededor de la línea de título de Fröhlich y Shepherdson; los otros dos títulos de la página (Yoshida, Auslander y Buchsbaum) no están enmarcados.
narratives.ar: الشكل 6: مسح ضوئي للصفحة 35 من المراجعات حيث رسم نموذج الرؤية الحاسوبية مربعاً أحمر واحداً (موسوماً بـ 'title') حول سطر عنوان Fröhlich وShepherdson؛ في حين لم يُحَط العنوانان الآخران في الصفحة (Yoshida، وAuslander وBuchsbaum) بأي مربع.
narratives.ru: Рисунок 6: скан страницы 35 с рефератами, на котором модель компьютерного зрения выделила одной красной рамкой (с меткой «title») строку заголовка статьи Fröhlich и Shepherdson, тогда как два других заголовка на странице (Yoshida, а также Auslander и Buchsbaum) остались невыделенными.
narratives.zh: 图 6：第 35 页评论扫描件，计算机视觉模型仅在 Fröhlich 与 Shepherdson 的标题行周围绘制了一个标有“title”的红框，而页面上的另外两个标题（Yoshida，以及 Auslander 与 Buchsbaum）未被框出。
